hook_text: Draw a rectangle. Add four lines at 45 degrees. Join them. The box just stood up off the page.
clip_script: Here is how a flat page holds a solid thing. Draw the front face true: a rectangle for a box. From each corner, a line up and right at 45 degrees, half as long as the real depth. Join the ends. That is cabinet oblique. Now the grammar. Thick line: an edge you can see. Thin: a guide. Dashed: something hidden behind. Chain: a centre. Scale 1:2 means half size on paper, but you write the real size, always. Dimensions: a thin line beside the edge, arrowheads touching thin extension lines, the number floating just above, each size exactly once. Title block at the bottom: name, date, scale, units. Next week the crane gets this treatment, and anyone who picks up the sheet can build it.
visual_style: Whiteboard rectangle sprouting 45 degree lines into a box; four line types drawn side by side; a dimension line with arrowheads appearing; a title block filling in.
mood: Calm and exact, a draughtsman at work.
pacing: Front, slant, join, lines, scale, dimensions, title block, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw a box at half scale in cabinet oblique.
